editorial:
Imagine you are watching a documentary about the adult film world, but things quickly take a dark turn. You follow a starlet who seems to be struggling with her life and career, and the whole thing feels very real because it is shot like a news report. The vibe is gritty and uncomfortable, making you feel like you are seeing something you aren't supposed to see. It starts off as a look into a taboo business, but it quickly turns into a mystery when the main girl dies on camera, leaving you wondering if what you saw was a stunt or something way worse.

What really works here is how the movie tricks you into thinking it is a true story. The acting is natural, and the slow build-up of tension keeps you on edge. While it can be a bit slow in some parts, the payoff is worth it. If you like movies that mess with your head, you should definitely give this a try. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, but if you are a big horror fan, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends by revealing that the whole documentary was a setup to cover up a real crime. You find out that the girl did not just kill herself, but was actually murdered as part of a snuff film. The filmmakers were actually the ones behind the horror. It wraps up by showing that the line between fake movies and real death is thinner than you think, leaving you with a cold feeling.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological tricks and old school horror.
